verdict.evidence: The kernel computes the gradient as tl.where(p > q, 0.5*scale, -0.5*scale) (tvd.py:89). At p == q this gives -0.5*scale. The float64 autograd of 0.5*|p-q| in reference.py uses sign(0) = 0, so the oracle gradient is 0 there. Any kept row with p[i,j] == q[i,j] therefore gets a wrong p.grad of -0.5*scale instead of 0. Using p = q makes every element tie, so the whole gradient is wrong. The loss, the scaling, the row masking and the reductions all look correct. I read the source only and did not run anything.
